A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ridge Boosting is Both Robust and Efficient. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo coverage results in Section 4.1 and an analysis of retirement income using 2018 American Community Survey data in Section 4.2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation and retirement-income results, including Figures 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The estimator remains an initial predictor followed by one kernel ridge regression step on its residuals. The objective, resulting predictor, and random-forest extension in Appendix B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate average-derivative estimation under the same three simulated environments and retirement-income profiles for ages 65-89 using the same 2018 American Community Survey data.

E2.justification: Both experiments retain the same comparison between naive kernel ridge regression and boosted kernel ridge regression. The newly cited related works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The simulation distributions, sample sizes of 50-500, symmetric-difference derivative estimation, and empirical application protocol remain unchanged. Replacing the malformed outcome expression 'Y = Y ~ f(X) + eta' with 'Y = f(X) + eta' corrects notation without substantively changing the stated data-generating process.

E4.justification: The same three-environment covariate-shift evaluation and retirement-income case study are retained. No ablations, sensitivity tests, error analyses, or additional empirical appendix analyses are introduced or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 Monte Carlo replications, nominal 95% asymptotic normal confidence intervals, empirical coverage, and retirement-income interval widths. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 2 have identical plotted content, and their accompanying findings are unchanged. Both versions report improved coverage with boosting and a flatter retirement-income profile than the naive estimate.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, results, and proofs remain substantively unchanged. v2 removes Appendix A.4's duplicate continuity and boundedness assumptions, references the identical existing Assumptions 1 and 2, and renumbers the remaining assumptions. The auditing-set subscript correction in Appendix A.2 is a notation fix.

C1.justification: The central claim remains simultaneous multiaccuracy and semiparametric efficiency for the specified RKHS class. v2 clarifies that density ratios lie in the RKHS unit ball in the abstract; this restriction was already explicit in v1's introduction and method discussion.

C2.justification: The Riesz-representer explanation, empirical interpretations, RKHS applicability restriction, and unresolved hyperparameter-tuning limitation are retained. Appendices B-D preserve the same qualifications and connections to random forests and TMLE.

D1.justification: The disclosed implementation information remains unchanged, including FolkTables processing, symmetric differencing, and execution of the simulation on a four-core laptop. No additional hyperparameters, implementation instructions, or code/data access information are supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds Globus-Harris et al. (2023) on multicalibration as boosting and Cho et al. (2024) on RKHS-based TMLE and universal adaptability. Brief discussion of potential unification with Cho et al. improves positioning without substantially restructuring the literature review.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the abstract, corrects spelling and equation references, cleans up the simulation outcome expression, and consolidates duplicate assumptions under 'Additional Assumptions.' The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Expanded related work and consolidated assumptions cause modest changes to text placement, equation spacing, and page breaks. Figures 1 and 2 retain their plots, axes, legends, captions, and placement; neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision and readability through the density-ratio clarification, corrected cross-references, and removal of duplicate assumptions. The two added related-work discussions improve attribution and positioning. The method, theoretical substance, and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited.
